title: Trading Halts
summary: What a pause does to price discovery, existing orders, and a derivative that may keep trading.
body_markdown:
A trading halt suspends some or all execution in a market. It does not suspend the arrival of information or guarantee that the next trade will occur near the last one. For a trader, the important consequence is the gap between having an opinion and being able to change a position.


Different pauses address different problems. A stock may stop while material news is released, because its price moves outside prescribed limits, or because a broader market mechanism has been triggered. Identify the reason before assuming how long the interruption will last or what can still trade.


## Price bands organize execution


The U.S.[Limit Up Limit Down plan](https://www.luldplan.com/) sets bands around a reference price for covered stocks during regular trading. Trades outside those bands are restricted, and a sustained limit state can lead to a pause. The rules are intended to manage trading conditions, not declare a company’s fundamental value.


A band therefore does not create a guaranteed floor for your holding. News can justify a lower price; the mechanism affects how execution proceeds while the market incorporates it. After the applicable pause and reopening process, the next executable price can differ substantially from the old one.


[Market-wide circuit breakers](https://www.nyse.com/trade/trading-information) are another arrangement. They reference specified declines in the S&P 500 and have rules that depend on severity and time of day. A market-wide interruption and an individual company’s news halt should not be treated as interchangeable events.


## A stop needs an executable market


Suppose a stock last traded at $100 and you have a sell stop with a $98 trigger. An announcement arrives during a halt, and the market next trades around $90. Under rules that trigger the stop on the reopening trade, a stop-market order becomes an instruction to sell at available prices. It does not entitle you to $98.


A stop-limit order makes a different tradeoff. A $98 trigger with a $97 limit can prevent execution below $97, but if all available bids are near $90, it may leave the position unsold. The price condition is preserved at the expense of certainty about exiting.


The precise trigger reference and treatment of orders belong to the venue and broker. Check whether orders remain queued, can be canceled, or participate in a reopening process. An old order confirmation is evidence that an instruction was accepted, not that it can execute during a suspension.


## Reopening is a new comparison of supply and demand


During a pause, traders can change their valuation and, where permitted, their instructions. A reopening auction brings eligible buying and selling interest together under the market’s rules. A displayed indication before reopening is not the same as a completed trade.


A large gap may look irrational when compared with the last print, yet be consistent with new information. Start with what changed in the business or market. The old price was formed with an earlier information set, and the absence of intervening transactions does not keep that set current.


## Related instruments may keep moving


A perpetual contract referencing a stock may operate while the stock exchange is closed or the stock is halted. That makes the contract available for trading; it does not guarantee that its market price, reference price, and eventual cash-stock price coincide throughout the interruption.


For a builder-deployed market, inspect the oracle, mark-price, and halt rules.[HIP-3](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hyperliquid-improvement-proposals-hips/hip-3-builder-deployed-perpetuals) includes a deployer-controlled halt action that cancels orders and settles positions using the current mark. That is a specific contract mechanism, distinct from a stock exchange reopening after a pause.


A position that can be traded continuously still needs enough collateral to withstand the prices its own venue uses. When underlying liquidity is interrupted, the gap between instruments can widen just when a trader most wants to reduce it. A continuously open screen removes the wait for an opening bell; it does not remove the risk that an exit is available only at a much worse price.
